title: Use colon for hierarchy and dot for variant in artifact names

facts.note: Any naming, referencing or reviewing of an artifact name where separator meaning matters; not limited to writing new names.
Task text mentions naming, referencing or reviewing artifacts.

values: artifact name containing ':' or '.' separators added, changed or referenced
facts.note: Needs an observer that extracts artifact names and emits a warning (not a hard failure) for any name with two or more dots, since multiple dots usually indicate over-specification.

values: separator misused (colon for a variant, dot for a deeper level)
facts.note: Whether a segment is a deeper level or a variant of the same thing is a semantic judgement.

fires: A new artifact name is introduced for a nested concept, e.g. a foundation under commons (colon-separated levels).
A state or flavor of an existing artifact is named (e.g. a raw form or active state) and dot must be chosen.
An existing or referenced artifact name chains several dots (e.g. .uuid.v7.encoded) and is reviewed for over-specification.
A review checks whether existing artifact names use colon and dot with their intended meaning.
doesNotFire: Work that neither names, references nor reviews artifact names.
Dots inside file names, file extensions, or code-level identifiers that are not artifact names.
Colons in prose or in YAML key/value syntax that are not part of an artifact name.

given: An artifact name whose colon (:) and dot (.) separators carry meaning
when: the artifact name is chosen, referenced or reviewed
then: Use colon (:) only for hierarchical descent to a deeper conceptual level, and dot (.) only for a lateral variation (flavor/state) of the same thing.
prefer: Colon for each step deeper into the resource tree; depth is unlimited (e.g. commons:ux:foundations:color, scenario:catalog:primitives:actor).
Keep dots shallow: typically one dot suffix for a variant of the same artifact (e.g. sensory:gesture.raw, player:session.active, match:config.duel), rarely two.
avoid: Chaining multiple dots (e.g. .uuid.v7.encoded) — this usually signals over-specification.
Using a dot to express a deeper conceptual level, or a colon to express a mere flavor/state of the same thing.
why: Colon is a strong boundary between different conceptual levels; dot is a soft boundary between facets at the same level. Keeping them distinct makes names navigable as a tree and keeps variants shallow.
evidence: Every colon in the artifact names in scope separates a different conceptual level (deeper in the resource tree).
Every dot segment denotes a flavor/state of the same thing at the same level.
Dot usage is shallow per the advisory guidance: typically one dot, rarely two; names with multiple dots are inspected as a likely sign of over-specification (warning, not a hard limit).
verifier_detail: Colon: purpose = hierarchical descent; multiplicity = unlimited; visual weight = strong boundary (different conceptual levels).
Dot: purpose = lateral variation; multiplicity = typically 1, rarely 2; visual weight = soft boundary (same level, different facet).
Warning heuristic: multiple dots (e.g. .uuid.v7.encoded) usually indicates over-specification — emit a warning for names with two or more dots; this is advisory, not a validity ceiling.
Positive colon examples: commons:ux:foundations:color, scenario:catalog:primitives:actor. Positive dot examples: sensory:gesture.raw, player:session.active, match:config.duel.
